I pieced together the layers from the final output. I did it by hand to avoid writing code. I saved it and picking it up here.


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

setwd(here::here('output','report files'))
df <- read.csv("report_i_made_from_risk_at_port_summary_layers.csv")
df$total_risk <- as.numeric(df$total_risk)

summ_1 <- df  |> dplyr::select(-layer_name, -point_count) |>  group_by(scenario, Container, PoE, Conveyance.type.pathway, Product.pathway, Product.subpathway) |> summarize(total_risk = sum(total_risk), na.rm = TRUE) |> ungroup() |> pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = total_risk)


summ_2 <- df |> group_by(scenario, PoE, Conveyance.type.pathway, Product.pathway, Product.subpathway) |> dplyr::select(-layer_name, -point_count, -Container) |> summarize(total_risk = sum(total_risk), na.rm = TRUE) |> pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = total_risk)

summ_3 <- df |> dplyr::select(-layer_name, -point_count, -Container, -PoE) |> group_by(scenario, Conveyance.type.pathway, Product.pathway, Product.subpathway) |> summarize(total_risk = sum(total_risk), na.rm = TRUE) |> pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = total_risk)


write.csv(summ_1, "summary_by_scenario.csv")
write.csv(summ_2, "summary_by_scenario_no_container.csv")
write.csv(summ_3, "summary_by_scenario_no_container_no_PoE.csv")

```

# trying some graphs

```{r sankey suggestion}
library(networkD3)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Assuming you're using the 'current' risk column
# Prepare the data for Sankey diagram
sankey_data <- summ_1 %>%
  dplyr::select(PoE, Product.pathway, Container, current) %>%
  filter(!is.na(current)) %>%
  # Create source-target pairs for the network
  mutate(
    PoE = paste0("PoE_", PoE),            # Prefix to avoid node name conflicts
    Product = paste0("Prod_", Product.pathway),
    Container = paste0("Cont_", Container)
  )

# Create nodes data frame
# All unique nodes from the three categories
nodes <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    unique(sankey_data$PoE),
    unique(sankey_data$Product),
    unique(sankey_data$Container)
  )
)
nodes$id <- 0:(nrow(nodes)-1)  # Zero-indexed node IDs

# Create links data frame
# First set of links: PoE to Product
links_poe_prod <- sankey_data %>%
  group_by(PoE, Product) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(current, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    source = match(PoE, nodes$name) - 1,
    target = match(Product, nodes$name) - 1
  )

# Second set of links: Product to Container
links_prod_cont <- sankey_data %>%
  group_by(Product, Container) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(current, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    source = match(Product, nodes$name) - 1,
    target = match(Container, nodes$name) - 1
  )

# Combine the links
links <- bind_rows(links_poe_prod, links_prod_cont) %>%
  dplyr::select(source, target, value)

# Create the Sankey diagram
sankeyNetwork(
  Links = links, 
  Nodes = nodes, 
  Source = "source", 
  Target = "target", 
  Value = "value", 
  NodeID = "name",
  fontSize = 12,
  nodeWidth = 30,
  sinksRight = FALSE,  # Set to TRUE if you want all "end" nodes on the right
  colourScale = JS("d3.scaleOrdinal().range(d3.schemeCategory20)"), # Color scheme
  height = 800,
  width = 1200
)

```{r sankey deus}
library(networkD3)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Prepare the data for Sankey diagram
sankey_data <- summ_1 %>%
  select(PoE, Container, Product.pathway, current) %>%
  filter(!is.na(current)) %>%
  # Create source-target pairs for the network
  mutate(
    PoE = paste0("PoE_", PoE),            # Prefix to avoid node name conflicts
    Container = paste0("Cont_", Container),
    Product = paste0("Prod_", Product.pathway)
  )

# Create nodes data frame - now ordering matters!
# Order as PoE -> Container -> Product
poe_nodes <- unique(sankey_data$PoE)
container_nodes <- unique(sankey_data$Container)
product_nodes <- unique(sankey_data$Product)

nodes <- data.frame(
  name = c(poe_nodes, container_nodes, product_nodes)
)
nodes$id <- 0:(nrow(nodes)-1)  # Zero-indexed node IDs

# Create first set of links: PoE to Container
links_poe_cont <- sankey_data %>%
  group_by(PoE, Container) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(current, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    source = match(PoE, nodes$name) - 1,
    target = match(Container, nodes$name) - 1
  )

# Second set: Container to Product
links_cont_prod <- sankey_data %>%
  group_by(Container, Product) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(current, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    source = match(Container, nodes$name) - 1,
    target = match(Product, nodes$name) - 1
  )

# Combine the links
links <- bind_rows(links_poe_cont, links_cont_prod) %>%
  select(source, target, value)

# Create the Sankey diagram with nodes ordered PoE -> Container -> Product
sankeyNetwork(
  Links = links, 
  Nodes = nodes, 
  Source = "source", 
  Target = "target", 
  Value = "value", 
  NodeID = "name",
  fontSize = 12,
  nodeWidth = 30,
  sinksRight = TRUE,  # Set to TRUE to enforce left-to-right flow
  colourScale = JS("d3.scaleOrdinal().range(d3.schemeCategory20)"), # Color scheme
  height = 800,
  width = 1200
)

````{r chord diagram}
library(circlize)
library(chorddiag)

# Create a matrix of flows between PoE and Product
chord_matrix <- summ_1 %>%
  select(PoE, Product.pathway, current) %>%
  filter(!is.na(current)) %>%
  group_by(PoE, Product.pathway) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(current, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Product.pathway,
    values_from = value,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("PoE") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Color by container type
container_colors <- summ_1 %>%
  select(PoE, Container) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  # Assign colors based on container
  mutate(color = case_when(
    Container == "baggage" ~ "#1f77b4",
    Container == "package" ~ "#ff7f0e",
    Container == "cargo" ~ "#2ca02c",
    Container == "mail" ~ "#d62728",
    TRUE ~ "#9467bd"
  ))

# Create the chord diagram
chorddiag(
  data = chord_matrix,
  groupColors = container_colors$color,
  groupnamePadding = 20,
  groupPadding = 3,
  showTicks = FALSE
)

```{r hierarchical_chord_diagram, fig.width=8, fig.height=8, dpi=100}
library(circlize)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(grid)
library(gridExtra)

# Prepare the data for hierarchical chord diagram
chord_data <- summ_1 %>%
  dplyr::select(PoE, Conveyance.type.pathway, Product.pathway, Product.subpathway, current) %>%
  filter(!is.na(current)) %>%
  # Create hierarchical groups
  mutate(
    # Create source group: PoE + Conveyance.type.pathway
    source_group = paste0(PoE, ":", Conveyance.type.pathway),
    # Create target group: Product.pathway + Product.subpathway
    target_group = paste0(Product.pathway, ":", Product.subpathway)
  ) %>%
  # Group by the new hierarchical categories and sum the values
  group_by(source_group, target_group) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(current, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Sort the data by value to improve visualization
chord_data <- chord_data %>% arrange(desc(value))

# Extract unique source and target groups
source_groups <- unique(chord_data$source_group)
target_groups <- unique(chord_data$target_group)

# Create a matrix for the chord diagram
chord_matrix <- chord_data %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = target_group,
    values_from = value,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("source_group") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Define custom grid colors based on the parent categories
source_parent_categories <- str_extract(rownames(chord_matrix), "^[^:]+")
target_parent_categories <- str_extract(colnames(chord_matrix), "^[^:]+")

# Get unique parent categories
all_parent_categories <- unique(c(source_parent_categories, target_parent_categories))

# Create a better color palette - using viridis for distinct colors
# and combining with RColorBrewer for a wider range
n_categories <- length(all_parent_categories)
viridis_colors <- viridis(min(9, n_categories), option = "D")
brewer_colors <- brewer.pal(min(9, n_categories), "Set1")
spectral_colors <- brewer.pal(min(11, n_categories), "Spectral")

# Combine color palettes if we have many categories
if (n_categories > 11) {
  parent_colors <- setNames(
    colorRampPalette(c(viridis_colors, brewer_colors, spectral_colors))(n_categories),
    all_parent_categories
  )
} else {
  # Use a mix of palettes for better distinction
  mixed_palette <- c(viridis_colors[1:min(5, n_categories)], 
                     brewer_colors[1:min(4, max(0, n_categories-5))],
                     spectral_colors[1:min(2, max(0, n_categories-9))])
  parent_colors <- setNames(mixed_palette[1:n_categories], all_parent_categories)
}

# Get colors for source and target groups
source_colors <- parent_colors[source_parent_categories]
target_colors <- parent_colors[target_parent_categories]

# Combine source and target colors
grid_colors <- c(source_colors, target_colors)

# Reset the circos environment
circos.clear()

# Parameters for better visualization
gap_degree <- 2  # Slightly reduced gap to use space more efficiently
transparency <- 0.7  # Transparency for better visibility
link_border <- "white"  # Border color for links
bg_color <- "#FCFCFC"  # Light background color

# Set up the plotting parameters - using equal margins to center the plot
par(mar = c(2, 2, 4, 2), bg = bg_color, cex = 1.1)

# Create the chord diagram with improved parameters for readability
circos.par(
  gap.degree = gap_degree,
  track.margin = c(0.03, 0.03),  # Slightly increased margin for better spacing
  start.degree = 90,
  clock.wise = FALSE,
  points.overflow.warning = FALSE,
  # More moderate canvas size to fit the page better
  canvas.xlim = c(-0.85, 0.85),  # Adjusted for better page fit
  canvas.ylim = c(-0.85, 0.85)   # Adjusted for better page fit
)

# Create the chord diagram with improved visual appeal
chordDiagram(
  chord_matrix,
  grid.col = grid_colors,
  transparency = transparency,
  link.border = link_border,
  link.lwd = 0.6,  # Slightly thicker links
  link.sort = TRUE,  # Sort links for better appearance
  link.largest.ontop = TRUE,  # Place largest flows on top
  annotationTrack = c("grid", "axis"),  # Add axis for scale reference
  preAllocateTracks = list(track.height = 0.12),  # Increased height  directional = 0,  # Removed directional arrows (was 1)
  # Removed direction-related parameters
  # link.arr.length and link.arr.width no longer needed
  # link.arr.col no longer needed
  annotationTrackHeight = c(0.05, 0.12),  # Height of annotation tracks
  diffHeight = 0.05,  # Increased height difference for sectors
  reduce = 0.01  # Small reduction factor to avoid overlaps
)

# Add custom labels with improved parent/child hierarchy formatting
circos.track(
  track.index = 1,
  panel.fun = function(x, y) {
    sector.name <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
    # Extract parent and child parts
    parts <- strsplit(sector.name, ":")[[1]]
    parent <- parts[1]
    child <- ifelse(length(parts) > 1, parts[2], "")
    
    xlim = get.cell.meta.data("xlim")
    ylim = get.cell.meta.data("ylim")
    
    # Get sector index to determine position in the circle
    sector.index = get.cell.meta.data("sector.numeric.index")
    total.sectors = get.cell.meta.data("num.sectors")
    
    # Calculate angle to determine the best text orientation
    sector_angle <- (sector.index / total.sectors) * 360
    
    # Choose text orientation based on position in the circle
    if (sector_angle > 90 && sector_angle < 270) {
      facing_direction <- "outside"
      adj_value <- c(0.5, 1)  # Adjust text position
      y_offset <- mm_y(-1)  # Move text away from circle
    } else {
      facing_direction <- "outside"
      adj_value <- c(0.5, 0)
      y_offset <- mm_y(2)  # Default position
    }
    
    # Adjust text size based on sector size and data value
    sector_size <- xlim[2] - xlim[1]
    sector_value <- sum(chord_matrix[sector.name,], na.rm=TRUE) + sum(chord_matrix[,sector.name], na.rm=TRUE)
    rel_importance <- sector_value / max(rowSums(chord_matrix) + colSums(chord_matrix), na.rm=TRUE)
    
    # Adjust text size based on sector size and importance
    text_cex <- min(1.0, max(0.65, sector_size/25 * (0.7 + 0.3*rel_importance)))
    
    # Position for the labels
    text_pos <- mean(xlim)
    
    # Format the label differently based on position and length
    # For all labels: show parent in bold, child in regular text with indentation
    
    # First line: Parent category (bold)
    circos.text(
      text_pos, ylim[1] + mm_y(3) + y_offset, 
      parent,
      cex = text_cex, adj = adj_value,
      facing = facing_direction, 
      niceFacing = TRUE,
      font = 2  # Bold font
    )
    
    if (child != "") {
      # Second line: Child category with indentation
      circos.text(
        text_pos, ylim[1] + mm_y(7) + y_offset, 
        paste0(" ", child),  # Add space for indentation
        cex = text_cex * 0.9, adj = adj_value,
        facing = facing_direction, 
        niceFacing = TRUE,
        col = "#404040"  # Dark gray for better visibility
      )
    }
  }
)

# Legend function is defined but not called - keeping it for future use if needed
create_custom_legend <- function() {
  # Create a transparent plotting area for the legend in top-right corner
  par(new = TRUE, fig = c(0.75, 0.98, 0.70, 0.95))
  plot.new()
  
  # Create a filled rectangle as background for the legend with more transparency
  rect(0, 0, 1, 1, border = NA, col = alpha("white", 0.85))
  
  # Increase number of columns to make the legend more compact
  num_cols <- min(4, ceiling(length(parent_colors) / 3))
  
  # Format the legend labels to be more concise
  legend_labels <- names(parent_colors)
  
  # Draw the legend with a border, smaller text size for compactness
  legend(
    "center",
    legend = legend_labels,
    fill = unname(parent_colors),
    title = "Categories",
    cex = 0.65,  # Smaller text size
    box.col = "#888888",
    box.lwd = 1,
    ncol = num_cols,
    bg = alpha("white", 0.9),
    title.col = "#333333",
    title.adj = 0.5
  )
}

# Legend is turned off - not calling create_custom_legend()

# Add a more informative and attractive title
title(
  main = "ASF Risk Flow: Hierarchical Pathway Analysis",
  sub = "Source: Port of Entry + Conveyance Type → Target: Product Pathway + Subpathway",
  cex.main = 1.2,  # Slightly smaller title to leave more room for diagram
  font.main = 2,
  col.main = "#333333",
  cex.sub = 0.8,  # Slightly smaller subtitle
  col.sub = "#555555",
  line = 0.5
)

# Add a caption with data information
mtext(
  text = paste0("Data shows relative risk flows between", 
                " hierarchical categories (n=", nrow(chord_data), ")"),
  side = 1, 
  line = 0.5,
  cex = 0.8,
  col = "#666666"
)
